targets.title: Interpersonal movement synchrony facilitates pro-social behavior in childrens peer-play.
targets.evidence_quote: As such, Tunçgenç & Cohen’s (2016b) measurement of social bonding behaviors will be employed to determine if the results can be replicated in the current study.
targets.outcome_quote: Despite findings from Tunçgenç & Cohen (2016b), the results from the current study reveal that interpersonal synchrony does not lead to increased instrumental helping and social bonding behaviors in three- to five-year-old children when paired with an adult partner.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contrast the absence of the central helping/social-bonding effect with the target. Limitations and exploratory empathy analyses do not replace that verdict.

reasoning: New child samples re-test the synchrony effects of Tunçgenç and Cohen (reference labeled 2016b). Kirschner and Tomasello supply the fish-feeding task and are not a separate target in the replication chain. DOI and author verify the matching completed thesis despite the catalog year difference.
